methods.name: register_candidate
methods.desc:
Admit a candidate (admin only). The directory_entry_id IS the candidate
key — one ID end to end. Locked once voting is open — candidates are fixed for the epoch (no additions/removals until finalize).

methods.name: admin_delete_candidate
methods.desc:
ESCAPE HATCH (admin only): delete one candidate box by id, unconditionally.
This is the guaranteed cure for any candidate_count / box-set desync, so the app can ALWAYS be driven to zero boxes and therefore ALWAYS deleted/closed — no ALGO is ever trappable behind an orphaned candidate box.
ALLOWED ONLY ONCE THE EPOCH IS OVER: either finalize has run (phase == 2), OR the tally round has arrived (Global.round >= tally_round) even if finalize has not yet succeeded. The second case (A-1) is the deadlock cure: if finalize ever can't run — e.g. a candidate_count/box-set desync makes the length check unsatisfiable — the app would otherwise be stuck in phase 0 with boxes that finalize can't delete and this hatch (phase-2-only) couldn't either, locking the pool forever. Permitting direct deletion from tally_round onward means the boxes are ALWAYS clearable, so finalize is never the sole path out.
It stays inert during the LIVE epoch (before tally_round), granting the admin NO mid-voting power: it cannot censor a not-yet-voted candidate, grief a project by front-running its first vote, or alter the ballot the public saw at registration. Since voting freezes at vote_close < tally_round, deletion only ever becomes possible after all voting has ended — the anti-censorship guarantee is fully preserved. A mistakenly-registered candidate simply sits at weight 0 through voting, is ignored by finalize, and is cleaned up afterward.
Returns the new candidate_count. The count floors at 0 even if it had drifted, so it can never underflow. Pair with a repeated off-chain enumeration of the app's boxes to clear every lingering candidate before admin_close.

methods.name: stake
methods.desc:
Group: [AssetTransfer Sprout -> app][this call]. Adds to staked balance.
Does NOT change any vote — the voter must re-vote to apply the new balance.

methods.name: unstake
methods.desc:
Return `amount` Sprout. Allowed any time (incl. after freeze). If the voter
has a vote, DECREMENT their voted weight (and the candidate) to match, so a candidate never holds more votes than real staked Sprout backing it.

methods.name: vote
methods.desc:
Back `candidate_id` with your FULL current staked balance. Window-only
(days 1–14). Snapshots your staked balance; re-vote to update after staking more. Changing candidate moves your weight from the old to the new. Returns the weight applied.

methods.name: tally
methods.desc:
PHASE 1 (admin). Caller submits all candidate ids sorted by weight DESC.
The contract VERIFIES the ordering against on-chain weights, derives the winner set itself (top ~TARGET_WINNERS, ties widen), FREEZES the pool and per-winner share, records each winner in a w: box, deletes all candidate boxes, and moves to phase 1 (awaiting payout). Returns the winner count.
Trustless ordering is preserved exactly as before: a dishonest ranking is rejected, and the winner set is the contract's own computation, not the caller's. Freezing the pool here (rather than at each payment) means the share can't drift as rewards arrive between payout transactions.

methods.name: pay_winners
methods.desc:
PHASE 2 (admin). Pay the next `count` winners their frozen share. Winner
payout addresses come from GLOBAL state (zero references), so this txn spends its reference budget only on the payout ACCOUNTS it pays — never on candidate or winner boxes. Idempotent via the paid_count cursor: a winner can never be paid twice, and the total paid can never exceed winner_count * share. Call repeatedly (slices of <= 8 to respect the account-reference limit) until paid_count == winner_count, then finish_tally.

methods.name: finish_tally
methods.desc:
PHASE 3 (admin). After every winner is paid, move to phase 2 so the next
epoch can open (and admin_close becomes reachable).
This is the guaranteed escape from phase 1: it requires only that all winners were paid (paid_count == winner_count), which pay_winners always makes reachable. Winner storage is GLOBAL state (no boxes), so there is nothing to orphan — clearing the scalars is enough; the stale winner addresses in w0..w7 are inert because winner_count returns to 0 and phase leaves 1.

methods.name: discard_unbootstrapped
methods.desc:
Delete an app that was CREATED but never bootstrapped (creator-only).
Guards the "created but bootstrap failed -> stuck forever" trap: before bootstrap, admin is the zero address, so admin_close's admin check can never pass and the app's ~1 ALGO funding would be stranded. This lets the original creator recover it. Strictly limited to the pre-bootstrap state (bootstrapped == 0) so it can NEVER run on a live governance app holding voter stake. Also safe on the ASA front: an unbootstrapped app never opted into Sprout, so there is no holding to clear — just close the ALGO account to the creator.

methods.name: admin_close
methods.desc:
Delete the app and recover funds (admin only). App B holds (not creates)
the Sprout ASA, so it opts out and closes cleanly — no manager needed.
SAFETY GATE: the app must hold ZERO Sprout (all voters unstaked) so close can never seize a voter's stake. The protocol also refuses to delete an app while ANY box still exists, and deleting with boxes present would permanently strand their MBR — so every candidate and voter box must be gone first. Voter boxes delete on full unstake; candidate boxes delete at tally, or individually via admin_delete_candidate (the escape hatch). candidate_count == 0 confirms the candidate set is cleared; if the counter ever disagrees with the real boxes, admin_delete_candidate can always drive both to zero, so the app — and its ALGO — can never be trapped. Winner storage is global state (no boxes), so it never blocks close. Not allowed mid-payout (phase 1): finish the payout (or force past it via the open_epoch recovery branch) first, so close never abandons an in-progress distribution. Operationally: unstake everyone, tally + pay + finish (or delete each candidate), confirm zero boxes off-chain, then close.
